title: "Elements of a Home Run"
subtitle: "Analyzing launch profiles and the physics of home runs using 2025 MLB Statcast data"

  echo: false

  message: false

::: {.lead}
What does it take to hit a home run in Major League Baseball? Using Statcast tracking data from the 2025 season, this interactive visualization examines how **exit velocity** and **launch angle** combine to send the ball over the fence.
:::

Hitting a home run requires a precise combination of swing mechanics and launch characteristics. Mechanically, a hitter generates explosive rotational power from the lower body through the hips and torso, delivering high bat speed along a slightly upward swing plane to make square contact on the lower half of the baseball. This collision creates the signature characteristics of a home run: an exit velocity typically topping 100 mph, a launch angle elevated into the 25°–35° window, and backspin that generates aerodynamic lift to carry the ball beyond outfield fences 380+ feet away.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: "100%"

library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

# Load Statcast data and format hover information for each home run
home_runs <- read_csv("data/home_runs_2025.csv") |>
  filter(!is.na(launch_speed), !is.na(launch_angle)) |>
  mutate(
    dist_label = if_else(is.na(hit_distance_sc), "N/A", paste0(hit_distance_sc, " ft")),
    hover_text = paste0(
      "<b>", player_name, "</b><br>",
      "Date: ", game_date, "<br>",
      "Matchup: ", away_team, " @ ", home_team, "<br>",
      "Exit Velocity: ", launch_speed, " mph<br>",
      "Launch Angle: ", launch_angle, "°<br>",
      "Distance: ", dist_label, "<br>",
      "Pitch: ", coalesce(pitch_name, "Unknown")
    )
  )

# Build plot with hover text on every point
p <- ggplot(home_runs, aes(x = launch_speed, y = launch_angle, color = hit_distance_sc, text = hover_text)) +
  geom_jitter(alpha = 0.45, size = 0.9, width = 0.4, height = 0.5) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "plasma", name = "Distance (ft)", na.value = "gray70") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(85, 125, by = 5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(15, 50, by = 5)) +
  labs(
    title = "Where Home Runs Happen: Exit Velocity vs. Launch Angle (2025)",
    subtitle = "Most home runs cluster between 100–110 mph exit velocity and 25°–35° launch angle",
    x = "Exit Velocity (mph)",
    y = "Launch Angle (degrees)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

# Convert ggplot to responsive plotly widget that fits the page
ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(autosize = TRUE) |>
  config(responsive = TRUE, scrollZoom = FALSE)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
### Key Insights from the Data

- **Exit Velocity (x-axis)**: The speed at which the ball leaves the bat in miles per hour. Most home runs require at least 95 mph, with the median hovering around 105 mph.
- **Launch Angle (y-axis)**: The vertical angle of the hit in degrees. The optimal trajectory for a home run falls between 25° and 35°.
- **Hit Distance (Color)**: Lighter yellow and orange tones represent tape-measure blasts (400+ ft), while darker purple points mark shorter hits that just cleared the fence.
- **The "Sweet Spot"**: Notice how the density of dots clusters heavily between **100–110 mph** and **25°–35°**. This combination produces the highest likelihood of a home run in Major League Baseball.
:::
